file_role: Every EXTERNAL number the TanitAD leaderboard may print, one row per number, each re-read from a BANKED primary (TanitAD Research Lab/Library, library key + table + PDF page). Consumed by `python -m taniteval.leaderboard build`. Our own numbers never live here: they come from taniteval/results/bench/**/summary.json, the registry and raw eval JSON.
owner: EvalFlyWheel W4 (leaderboard generator) — exclusive write; W6 (nuScenes) contributes rows via a patch file

verification.rule: for every row: the PDF's sha256 must equal library.json, and every string in `page_tokens` must occur in the PyMuPDF text of `source.page` (1-based PDF page index). A value that cannot be found on its cited page FAILS. A deliberate-regression arm perturbs every value and must fail on every row.

EPDMS_v2_navhard_two_stage.title: NAVSIM v2 — navhard two-stage EPDMS (the OFFICIAL column)
EPDMS_v2_navhard_two_stage.definition: Two-stage pseudo-simulation on navhard: 450 stage-1 and 5,462 stage-2 observations (2506.04218 p.7). Official leaderboard: HF space AGC2025/e2e-driving-navhard.
EPDMS_v2_navhard_two_stage.tanitad_pending: navhard_two_stage bytes are on D: (sha256 == HF ETag, BUILD_PLAN §0); the metric cache builds after A8; our model inference waits for a GPU gap (PI 2026-09-19). Fills from taniteval/results/bench/navsim_v2/navhard_two_stage/<run_id>/summary.json (W1 contract).
EPDMS_v2_navhard_two_stage.route_oracle: ⚠️ ROUTE-LEVEL ORACLE: NavSim's driving command is derived from the expert's driven path at roadblock granularity, and on stage 2 the command and route are copied from the expert's own frame (5,462/5,462 navhard; W2 D-NAVSIM-ROUTE-LEAK). It is NOT a trajectory leak — and ⛔ no route-following skill may be claimed from a command-conditioned row.
EPDMS_v2_navhard_two_stage.sample_overlap: ⛔ 367 of navhard's 450 stage-1 tokens are navtest tokens, and warmup ⊂ navhard (16/16) — the navhard, navtest and warmup columns are NOT independent samples of each other (W2 D-NAVSIM-SPLIT-NESTING).
EPDMS_v2_navhard_two_stage.stop_floor_rule: ⛔ EVERY NavSim ROW NEEDS ITS **STOP** FLOOR BESIDE CV — on v1 and v2 alike, and both generations have now MEASURED it: **navhard STOP 29.85 vs CV 11.48 (2.6x)**, **navtest STOP 61.82 vs CV 20.65 (3.0x)**. Mechanism, from source and confirmed by the run: the split keeps only scenes the HUMAN passes, so a stopped ego holds NC / DAC / TTC near 1 — **5/12 = 41.67 PDMS points free** — plus comfort at low speed. ⇒ CV is not the floor it looks like, and on v1 it is also the agent the split was FILTERED with, so it cannot be read as a generic floor at all. ⭐ The 20-token smoke that first showed this is SUPERSEDED by the full 12,146-token run; its numbers were never printed here and the full-split values are in the table below.

nuScenes_OL_L2_stp3.title: nuScenes open-loop planning — ST-P3 convention (L2 averaged up to t)
nuScenes_OL_L2_stp3.definition: Averaged-up-to-t reduction (ST-P3 metrics.py; VAD metric_stp3.py; AD-MLP re-uses ST-P3's code) — NUSCENES_PROTOCOL.md §5.2. BEV-Planner (2312.03031) re-scores every method with one implementation and a 0.1 m grid: same L2 convention, a DIFFERENT collision implementation — rendered as its own sub-table (`implementation`), never in the same column. ⛔ Inadmissible as a TanitAD criterion (H-EVAL-6 SUPPORTED; D-BENCH-PORT SKIP claim-bearing).
nuScenes_OL_L2_stp3.tanitad_pending: NOT RUN — no bytes. When it runs: `python -m taniteval.bench nuscenes_ol --ckpt <path> --split val (ONE run per convention)`, one run per convention, and it is comparable ONLY with the ego-status-free rows - nus.bevp.uniad_noego (1.03), nus.bevp.vad_noego (1.25), nus.bevp.bev_planner (0.55) - because our binding rule forbids ego status at inference and our arm is command-free.
nuScenes_OL_L2_stp3.harness_note: ⛔ THE HARNESS VERSION, NOT THE METHOD, MOVES THESE NUMBERS — there is no devkit here, so the harness IS the research codebase. the same VAD checkpoint reads 0.72 m under VAD's harness and 1.22 m with the averaging removed (paradrive-cvpr2024 Tab. 1), and the UniAD/VAD ranking flips between the two legacy harnesses (Tab. 8). Our own runs carry (reduction, pipeline) on every row for exactly this reason. Reduction pinned to OpenDriveLab/ST-P3@69aabefd2610951d9e34238142776ed2228673be evaluate.py:71-73,135-137,166; VAD@1688c4b1c3a9e2e7873ca9700ff8058170c0e3c8 metric_stp3.py; AD-MLP@4b93ba085ee47474152f282177865796ea577fc0 re-uses ST-P3's code (deps/stp3). (W6, MEASURED-from-source). Collision implementations in the field: 0.5 m grid, axis-aligned ego box — ST-P3 / UniAD / VAD (the legacy rows); 0.1 m grid, estimated yaw, trajectory-level — BEV-Planner (2312.03031); box-vs-box polygons, estimated yaw — SparseDrive (2405.19620) and DiffusionDrive; oriented box, 0.1 m, first frame removed — PARA-Drive (code not released).
nuScenes_OL_L2_stp3.command_note: ⚠️ COMMAND IS GT-DERIVED on every published row — GT-derived: the high-level command is the GT future's final lateral offset thresholded at +-2 m (VAD vad_nuscenes_converter.py:452-457, UniAD trajectory_api.py:272-280, ST-P3 NuscenesData.py:525-530, SparseDrive models/motion/decoder.py:167-173 - MEASURED-from-source at the pinned commits). No command-following skill may be claimed from such a row.
nuScenes_OL_L2_stp3.gt_control_note: ⛔ READ THE FLOOR BEFORE THE RANKING: the recorded HUMAN driver 'collides' 0.36 % under the UniAD methodology and 0.96 % under VAD's, and exactly 0.00 % once the ego box is oriented on a 0.1 m grid (paradrive-cvpr2024 Tab. 8 / Tab. 2). ⇒ no collision number within ~2× of its own protocol's floor is readable, and the AV rows EXCLUDE steps where the GT box collides (PARA-Drive fn. 4), so an in-protocol GT arm scores 0 by construction. The GT-human rows are carried in the tables as controls.
